title: Trust Architecture: Three-Act Seller Storyline (deck draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact seller-facing slide deck to guide a 10–15 minute technical+business conversation that builds trust with platform teams and security stakeholders. Focus: how Redwood mitigates operational risk during pilot→prod for private and dedicated deployments.

Slide 1 — Title + Hook:
- Title: Trust Architecture: Three-Act Seller Storyline
- One-liner: From unknown model behavior to production confidence — a repeatable pilot story you can run in 30 days.
- Speaker note: Start with a 25s narrative — "We focus on removing the two things that keep infra/platform teams up at night: unpredictable cost and unpredictable downtime."

Slide 2 — Why trust matters (quick framing)
- Bullet: Enterprise teams buy durability and predictable failure modes, not just best-average latency.
- Bullet: Private deployments add control but also surface ops ownership questions.
- Quick stat: Typical pilot failure causes: integration gaps (41%), SLO mismatches (27%), cost surprises (18%). [internal metric placeholder]
- Speaker note: Use a past customer vignette (anonymized) where a cached KV issue surfaced only under load — we turned it into a repeatable canary test.

Slide 3 — Act 1: Set the stage (context + buy-in)
- Goal: Align on acceptable SLOs, sensitive data boundaries, and deployment model (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Seller script: "Before we talk models, what does success look like for your ops team in the first 90 days?"
- Assets to drop: one-page risk matrix, minimal network diagram, pilot success criteria template (link).
- Notes-to-self: Ask about CI/CD integration early — where will their infra want tracing hooks?

Slide 4 — Act 2: The Tension (risks we’ll neutralize)
- List of common buyer fears as headlines: Data exfiltration, Cost spikes, Latency cliffs under load, Model regressions, Rollback complexity.
- For each fear, one-line mitigation: e.g., Data exfiltration → VPC private endpoints + KMS/HSM keys in customer control.
- Mini-case: fallback routing applied when Dedicated capacity saturates — reduced error rate from 7% → 1.2% in trial.

Slide 5 — Act 2b: Live demo outline (for SE prep)
- Two demo kernels: 1) Private deployment onboarding script (network + key exchange). 2) Canary that simulates KV cache invalidation and shows automatic fallback to a compatible variant.
- SE checklist: tokens-per-second metric exposed, cost-per-100k-tokens estimate, tracing correlation ids.
- TODO: record short 2-minute screen capture of failover path.

Slide 6 — Act 3: Resolution (evidence & commitments)
- Evidence types we bring: SLA draft, per-token cost transparency, A/B quality evaluation for fallback models, runbook excerpt for incident handoffs.
- Seller line: "If you want it in writing, here’s a 30-day pilot statement of work with clear exit criteria."
- Include pilot timeline: Week 0 onboarding, Week 1 canary + smoke tests, Week 2 dataset-level quality checks, Week 3 scale run, Week 4 handoff + optional Dedicated reservation proposal.

Slide 7 — Objection handling cheat sheet (copyable lines)
- "We’re worried about cost unpredictability": "We provide per-route token breakdowns and two control levers — burst-cap limits and prefix/KV caching configs — to bound spend."
- "Our security team requires HSM-managed keys": "Redwood integrates with common KMS/HSM providers; we can do key-wrapping flows during onboarding."
- "We can’t tolerate model regressions": "We run evals on your prompt set pre/post rollout and gate by perf delta thresholds; automatic rollback policy available."

Slide 8 — Quick technical appendix (single-screen)
- Bullet: Supported network topologies (VPC peering, PrivateLink, on-prem appliance).
- Bullet: Observability hooks: per-request trace id, token-level billing lineitems, per-route latency percentiles.
- Bullet: Fallback policy primitives: variant routing, quantized fallbacks, region failover.

Slide 9 — Pilot success metrics (example targets)
- Availability target: 99.95%
- P95 generation latency target: < 250ms for x tokens (config dependent)
- Cost delta vs baseline: < 15% during pilot with caching enabled
- Quality delta: human-eval pass rate >= baseline - 2%
- Notes: Replace with account-specific numbers before sending.

Slide 10 — Handoff checklist (ops-friendly deliverables)
- Network diagram + endpoints, KMS key fingerprints, Canary test script, Per-route SLOs, Incident runbook excerpt, Contact list for on-call engineers.
- Owner actions: SE to collect network CIDR within 48h; Solutions engineer to schedule a 60-minute runbook dry-run in week 3.

Slide 11 — Quick roleplay scripts (30s each)
- Seller opener -> SE tech validation -> Security champion: short sample dialogue with prompts to escalate to legal if needed.
- Example: Seller: "At a high level, we isolate traffic into your VPC and maintain no persistent access to your keys." Security champion: "How are keys rotated?" SE: "We provide an automated rotation plan that mirrors your KMS policy and show rotation logs during the dry-run."

Slide 12 — Appendix: Evidence pack links (placeholders)
- Pilot SOW sample: confluence link
- One-pager on caching and microbatch economics: confluence link
- Recorded canary demo: internal recording link (TODO)

Slide 13 — Risks & open questions (notes-to-self)
- Does the prospect have strict egress rules that prevent outbound telemetry? If yes, note alternative: push-only logs into customer S3.
- Who owns the rollback decision in their change control? Add as acceptance criterion in SOW.
- Action: request list of top 20 prompts the app will use for pre-rollout evals.

Slide 14 — Next steps / CTA (one-line)
- Ask for a 60-minute pilot kickoff meeting. Offer to run a technical dry-run in the first week.
- Optional CTA for finance: preliminary reservation sketch if sustained usage looks likely.

Notes (internal draft voice):
- Keep this deck intentionally short — target 10 slides + appendix.
- Make a 1-page PDF variant for security stakeholders (condensed evidence + SOW highlights).
- Cross-link to "pilot-template-v2" in Confluence.
- Follow-up TODOs: record demo, update SLA draft with legal (Rae), finalize SOW template (Liam).

Known limitations / work-in-progress:
- Need verified latency baselines for the new quantized variants (tracking in JIRA-6543).
- Sample Canaries: not yet recorded; schedule with infra lab (Marco).

Speaker reminders: keep language operational and non-marketing, surface explicit acceptance criteria early, and always close with a single next step (pilot kickoff).
